clue.text: Driver, English, at home with Englishman

parts.note: Eng is the standard abbreviation for English
someone at home is in
E for English plus MAN

explanation.surface: A chauffeur who is English, staying home with a fellow Englishman.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine-man operates an engine, especially a railway locomotive, so he is its driver.

clue.text: Football manager should pick half of you

definitions.note: a description: what a manager ought to choose
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the correct team, the one a manager ought to select
second meaning: the right-hand half of a person's body

explanation.surface: A fan telling the manager to choose half of the reader for the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side' is a team in British usage, so a good manager picks the right one; your body also has a right half and a left half.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both the correct team to field and the right-hand half of the human body.

clue.text: Some of the best Irishmen are in clink

indicators.note: 'some of' says only a portion of the following words is needed

parts.note: runs across the end of 'best' and the start of 'Irishmen'

explanation.surface: A sour remark that many fine Irishmen end up in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir and clink are both slang words for prison.

clue.text: Grimy cans he destroyed. Great pity!

indicators.note: something destroyed is wrecked, so these letters are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: the eleven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone crushed some dirty tins, and what a waste that was.
explanation.definitionFit: A crying shame is an idiom for something deeply regrettable, so it equals a great pity.

clue.text: Law upset Egyptian godhead

indicators.note: upset things are knocked about, so the remaining letters are rearranged
read 'godhead' as a god's head, its first letter, which is lopped off

parts.note: with the god of the next word, an Egyptian deity, strictly a goddess, of love and music

explanation.surface: A legal code that overthrew the divinity worshipped in ancient Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Godhead' looks like one word for divinity, but it splits into god and head, the instruction to drop the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Torah is the Jewish Law, the first five books of the Hebrew Bible.

clue.text: Cotton cloth is a bore

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a strong twilled cotton fabric
second meaning: a tool for boring holes

explanation.surface: Someone finds cotton fabric tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' reads as a dull thing, but it is the boring tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Drill is both a hard-wearing twilled cotton fabric and a tool that bores holes.

clue.text: Somehow it can make a trick

indicators.note: 'somehow' says the letters get there by some unstated route, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the five letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wonders how a simple 'it can' could amount to a conjuring trick.
explanation.definitionFit: An antic is a playful or grotesque caper, a prank, so it serves as a noun for a trick.

clue.text: Brilliant managers, right for forward-looking navy

parts.note: a star performer is brilliant
the board of directors manages a company

explanation.surface: Praise for a navy's clever commanders, with a nod to seeing what lies ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a little riddle: a sailor facing the bow has the right-hand side of the ship on the right, and that side is called STARBOARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Starboard is the nautical term for the right-hand side of a vessel as seen by someone looking towards the bow.

clue.text: Oarsmen had some food, so they say

indicators.note: 'so they say' points to what people pronounce, so the sound of the phrase matters, not its spelling

parts.note: to have had some food is to have eaten, the past tense of eat

explanation.surface: The rowing crew stopped for a meal, or so rumour has it.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing eight is a rowing boat with eight oarsmen, and the crew itself is called an eight.

clue.text: Cross provides one bishop with one piece of furniture

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
Right Reverend, the title of a bishop, abbreviated RR
'with' adds a second Roman numeral one
a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: A church supplier offers a crucifix along with a bishop's chair or desk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like the Christian symbol beside the bishop, but it is the adjective meaning angry. RR stands for Right Reverend, a bishop's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cross is annoyed, and an irritable person is quick to anger: both describe a bad temper.

clue.text: Several free kicks observed in the quad

definitions.note: a description of what a quad has, not a synonym

parts.note: four is a specimen of several
corner kicks, set pieces awarded in football

explanation.surface: A referee awarding a string of free kicks in a school quadrangle game.
explanation.walkthrough: A quad, a quadrangle, is a four-sided courtyard, so it has four corners. A corner is strictly a set piece rather than a free kick.
explanation.definitionFit: A quadrangle is four-sided, so the four corners are just what anyone standing in it can see.

clue.text: Get cow's meat cooked in London home

indicators.note: food that is cooked is changed from its raw state, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: the eleven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Buy some beef and have it roasted back at your London house.
explanation.walkthrough: A mews is a London back street of former stables, now converted into small, sought-after houses.
explanation.definitionFit: A mews cottage is a converted stable dwelling typical of London's mews streets, so it is a kind of London home.

clue.text: Route taken by leader of the guard

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
a rail guards a drop or a stair

explanation.surface: The path a guard's commander follows on patrol.
explanation.definitionFit: A trail is a path or track, a route through country.

clue.text: That chap will vigorously pursue the demon

parts.note: he'll, short for he will
to hound someone is to chase them relentlessly

explanation.surface: A man vowing to chase down the devil himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A hellhound is a fiendish dog of hell, and by extension a fiend or demonic person.

clue.text: Guard heads of antenatal clinic in Pacific coast city

indicators.note: 'in' places the selected letters inside the city's name

parts.note: a familiar short name for the big Californian port city by the Golden Gate
the setter treats this as ante-natal, two words, taking the head of each

indicators.note: the heads of words are their front letters

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Security staff protecting the senior staff of a maternity clinic in a West Coast city.
explanation.walkthrough: Francisco is a sentinel in Shakespeare's Hamlet, on guard at Elsinore in the opening scene. Taking two heads from 'antenatal' relies on its older spelling ante-natal.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hamlet, Francisco is the soldier standing watch when Bernardo arrives to relieve him, so he is a guard.

clue.text: Shakespeare would be dull if read backwards

indicators.note: reading backwards takes the letters from right to left

parts.note: drab means dull and colourless

explanation.surface: A cheeky claim that the great playwright would be boring if you read him in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare is known as the Bard, a poet's title, so the word stands in for him.

clue.text: This fish would be opened up in bed

parts.words: would be opened up in bed
parts.note: surface reading: a fish split open for cooking while lying in bed

parts.words: would be opened up in bed
parts.note: setter's reading: write the fish inside the word bed, between B and ED, and the result means opened up, as a cask or a subject is opened

explanation.surface: A fish that would be gutted where it lies in a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: B + ROACH + ED makes BROACHED, and to broach is to open up. The clue describes what happens when the fish's name is put in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The roach is a common European freshwater fish of the carp family, a staple of coarse angling.

clue.text: Colour of the crucifix

indicators.note: 'of' marks the colour as being made from part of the following words

parts.note: found spanning the end of 'the' and the start of 'crucifix'

explanation.surface: Asking what shade a crucifix is painted.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecru is a pale greyish-yellow or beige shade, the tint of unbleached linen.

clue.text: Mollusc-seller and prostitute, unaccompanied, coming round my turning

parts.note: moll is old slang for a prostitute

indicators.note: something turning faces the other way, so the word my is written back to front

parts.note: taken as written
unaccompanied means on one's own

explanation.surface: A seafood hawker who doubles as a streetwalker, working alone, turning up on my patch.
explanation.walkthrough: The order is loose: the reversed word sits between the two other pieces. Molly Malone is the Dublin street-seller of the song, wheeling 'cockles and mussels', and legend makes her a part-time prostitute too.
explanation.definitionFit: Molly Malone of the folk song sold cockles and mussels, which are shellfish, so she is a seller of molluscs.

clue.text: Is it safer if you dispel them?

definitions.text: Is it safer if you dispel them?

parts.words: Is it safer if you dispel them?
parts.note: surface reading: whether getting rid of some danger makes you safer
setter's reading: what you dispel are worries, and losing them only makes you feel safer, which is the question

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a riddle about anxieties: dispelling them changes how safe you feel, not how safe you are.
explanation.definitionFit: Fears are anxieties or apprehensions, things one is said to dispel when reassured.

clue.text: To erect sounds destructive

indicators.note: 'sounds' says the answer is heard as another word, so pronunciation counts here

parts.note: to raze is to destroy a building completely

explanation.surface: Building something up can sound like demolition.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words are opposites that sound the same: one puts a building up, the other knocks it flat.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise a building or a mast is to set it upright, to erect it.

clue.text: Aid to memory includes one that will be left

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a reminder jogs the memory
a means one

explanation.surface: A note to self that lists what you will leave behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A remainder is whatever remains or is left over once the rest has been taken away.

clue.text: Impetuosity shown by tailless antelope

indicators.note: without a tail means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: the eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: An antelope that has lost its tail charges about rashly.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is dash and impetuous vigour, the quality of rushing in with spirit.

clue.text: Day for dressin' up?

definitions.note: a first name that goes with the surname Day
definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... Day, the British television interviewer, so his first name

definitions.note: read as the dropped-g verb robin', putting on robes
definitions.meaning: second meaning: with the final g dropped as the apostrophe shows, robing is dressing up in robes

explanation.surface: Asking which day of the year is set aside for putting on your finery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Day' looks like a date on the calendar but is a surname. Sir Robin Day was a famous BBC political interviewer. The apostrophe in dressin' tells you to drop a final G.
explanation.definitionFit: Robing means putting on robes, a formal kind of dressing up; shorn of its g it matches the given name.

clue.text: Where cars' doors might get shattered?

definitions.text: Where cars' doors might get shattered?

indicators.note: shattered things lie in broken pieces, so these letters are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A spot where car doors are likely to be smashed in collisions.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: crossing traffic makes a junction a place where side doors get hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossroad is a junction where two roads cross, a classic site of side-on collisions.

clue.text: I'm cut: it's the very devil when getting old

definitions.note: the answer speaks of itself: I am a cut

parts.note: the contracted 's of it's, standing for is

parts.words: the very devil when getting old
parts.note: Old Nick is a traditional name for the Devil, and the 'old' says which name

explanation.surface: An old person's lament that a cut is a real nuisance at their age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When getting old' points to Old Nick, the Devil's nickname, and supplies only the 'old' that tells you which name. A snick is a small cut or nick.
explanation.definitionFit: A snick is a small notch or nick, so the answer can say of itself that it is a cut.
